name: SwipeItem
description: A list item that slides aside to show the commands under it — Mail's archive and delete.

props.name: children
props.description: The item's parts, exactly as in a `List.Item`: `List.Media`, `List.Content`, `List.End`, `List.Actions`.

props.name: startActions
props.description: `SwipeItem.Action`s under the inline start edge — a swipe towards the end of the line reveals them. The first is outermost.

props.name: endActions
props.description: `SwipeItem.Action`s under the inline end edge — a swipe towards the start reveals them. The first is outermost.

props.name: fullSwipe
props.description: A swipe carried most of the way across performs the outermost action instead of stopping at the tray — iOS's archive.

props.name: open
props.description: Which tray is open. Controlled; `null` is closed.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Which tray is open to begin with.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Which tray is open now, and why: a `swipe`, `focus`, an `outside-pointer` press, `escape`, or an `action` chosen.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Lets the item's parts wrap onto a second line, as on `List.Item`.

props.name: selected
props.description: Tints the item as chosen, as on `List.Item`.

props.name: chevron
props.description: Ends the item with a chevron, as on `List.Item`.

parts.name: SwipeItem.Action
parts.description: One command in a tray: a label, and an icon over it if there is one.

props.name: children
props.description: What it does, in a word: "Archive", "Delete". It is the button's name.

props.name: icon
props.description: An icon over the label. Decoration — the label names the button.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Runs the command. The tray closes after it unless `closeOnSelect` is `false`.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description: Whether choosing the action closes the tray. Default `true`.

keyboard.action: Reaches the tray's actions after the item's own, opening the tray they are in.
Closes an open tray and returns focus to the item's action.

a11y: A swipe is a shortcut, not the only way in. The actions are real buttons in the tab order, after the item's own action, and focus reaching one opens its tray — so a keyboard and a screen reader find them without swiping. A path-based gesture still needs a non-path way for a pointer (WCAG 2.5.1): offer the same commands where a press reaches them too, on the item's own page or in a `Menu` in `List.Actions`.
